policy: An adjudication pins the SHA-256 of ONE exact value. It is deliberately not a path rule: exempting one adjudicated test vector does not exempt any other value, in that file or anywhere else, so this file cannot be used to smuggle a real credential past the scan. Every entry must carry a reason and an adjudicating task; an entry missing either is reported as a failure rather than honoured.
why_this_exists: An INDEPENDENT AUDIT showed the scanner's earlier blanket test-path exemption returned True for a credential-shaped value, which would have waved a real key through. Fixing that made the scanner flag the audit report itself, because that report quotes the scanner's own test vector as evidence. Redacting the evidence and re-exempting the path were both rejected: the first destroys evidence, the second reopens the hole. Pinning the digest of the single adjudicated value closes both.

adjudications.reason: Synthetic test vector, not a credential. It is the string this repository's own secret-scan self-test uses, and the independent audit quotes it while demonstrating the exemption defect it found. Exempting the exact value is safe because the exemption is pinned to these bytes.
adjudications.review_condition: Remove once the audit report is archived out of reports/current.
